facts.statement: The name Auroraceratops honors Dawn Dodson, wife of co-author Peter Dodson, and its status as an early ceratopsian.
facts.quote: The etymology of the generic name refers to its status as an early ceratopsian and also to Dawn Dodson, wife of Peter Dodson, one of the palaeontologists who described it.

facts.statement: A well-preserved skull was recovered in 2004 from the Gongpoquan Basin and accessioned as CAGS IG-2004-VD-001.
facts.quote: A well-preserved skull of an early ceratopsian was recovered in 2004 by fieldwork of the FRDC in the Gongpoquan Basin, and accessioned as CAGS IG-2004-VD-001.

facts.statement: The species Auroraceratops rugosus was named in 2005, with CAGS IG-2004-VD-001 designated as the holotype.
facts.quote: You and colleagues chose to name the new binomial Auroraceratops rugosus for the specimen in 2005, making CAGS IG-2004-VD-001 the holotype of their new taxon.

facts.statement: At least 50 specimens were found in 2007, and the total count of individuals reached 80 by the end of the 2010 field season.
facts.quote: A series of at least 50 well-preserved specimens of Auroraceratops were recovered in the late summer of 2007, and excavations in subsequent seasons by the FDRC, Gansu Geological Museum (GGM) and University of Pennsylvania among other institutions brought the count of individuals of Auroraceratops to 80 by the end of the 2010 field season.

facts.statement: A specimen named GGM-FV-00500 was described in 2012 as a potential new species but lacked sufficient data for a formal name.
facts.quote: One specimen from this area, GGM-FV-00500, was described in 2012 by You and colleagues, who considered it to represent a new species of Auroraceratops, but lacked data to justify giving it a name.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops has a shorter, wider snout compared to the long, narrow snouts of most other neoceratopsians.
facts.quote: Though most other neoceratopsians are characterized by a long, narrow snout, Auroraceratops has a shorter wider one.

facts.statement: The skull of Auroraceratops is flat and wide, measuring 20 cm in length.
facts.quote: The 20 cm skull itself is rather flat and wide.

facts.statement: Paired rugose areas, likely covered in keratin, were located in front of the eyes and on the jugal and lower jaw.
facts.quote: Paired rugose areas, very probably covered in keratin in life, are in front of the eyes and on the jugal with corresponding areas on the lower jaw.

facts.statement: A 2019 analysis estimated Auroraceratops was a bipedal animal 1.25 m long, with a hip height of 44 cm and a body mass of 15.5 kg.
facts.quote: A detailed analysis of the post-cranial skeleton published in 2019 showed that the animal would have walked bipedally and had an estimated length of 1.25 m, hip height of 44 cm and body mass of 15.5 kg.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Auroraceratops died by rapid burial inside burrows, indicated by curled-up preservation and lack of weathering.
facts.quote: The bone beds of articulated Auroraceratops specimens (1869 skeletal elements from 74 individuals) indicate that these individuals died by rapid burial inside burrows based on its preservation in a curled up position and lack of bone weathering.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops is found in the red beds of the Zhonggou Formation alongside Archaeoceratops oshimai, Beishanlong, Suzhousaurus, and an unnamed ornithomimosaur.
facts.quote: Auroraceratops is only known from the red-colored beds that form the bottom of the Zhonggou Formation, where it has been found alongside Archaeoceratops oshimai, Beishanlong and the unnamed ornithomimosaur, and Suzhousaurus and "N." bohlini.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops is notable as the first relatively large ceratopsian found in Asia.
facts.quote: Este hallazgo ha sorprendido a científicos porque Auroraceratops es el primer ceratopsiano relativamente grande hallado en Asia.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops is classified within the infraorder Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: infraordo: Ceratopsia

facts.statement: Auroraceratops belongs to the unranked family Neoceratopsia.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Neoceratopsia

facts.statement: Auroraceratops was a moderate-sized ceratopsian dinosaur about 2 meters long.
facts.quote: Auroraceratops fue un ceratópsido de tamaño moderado de unos 2 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops was a bipedal dinosaur characterized by bony rugosities on its face and jaw.
facts.quote: Era un bípedo que se caracterizaba por poseer rugosidades óseas en su cara y mandíbula.

facts.statement: Unlike most other neoceratopsians with long, narrow snouts, Auroraceratops had a short and wide snout.
facts.quote: Aunque la mayoría de los otros neoceratopsianos son caracterizados por un hocico largo y estrecho, Auroraceratops lo tiene ancho y corto.

facts.statement: The skull of Auroraceratops measured around 20 centimeters, being somewhat flat and wide with a narrower base.
facts.quote: El cráneo en sí mismo mide alrededor de 20 centímetros, es algo plano y ancho con una base más estrecha.

facts.statement: The profile of Auroraceratops' short, high, and rounded snout resembles that of a turtle.
facts.quote: El perfil de su corto, alto y redondeado hocico recuerda al de una tortuga.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops had at least two pairs of striated ridges on its simple, nearly cylindrical premaxillary teeth, a characteristic of neoceratopsians.
facts.quote: Tienen por lo menos dos pares de rebordes estriados en los dientes premaxilares son simples y casi cilíndricos, que es una característica neoceratopsianos.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops possessed paired rugose areas, likely covered in keratin during life, located in front of the eyes and on the jugal, with corresponding areas on the lower jaw.
facts.quote: Las áreas rugosas apareadas, cubiertas muy probablemente en queratina en vida, están delante de los ojos y en el yugal con áreas correspondientes en la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: The rugose structures on Auroraceratops were likely used for inter- and intraspecific interactions.
facts.quote: Estas rugosidades eran probablemente utilizadas para las interacciones inter e intraespecíficas.

facts.statement: A possible function for Auroraceratops' rugose structures was in social dominance conflicts and mating rituals involving pushing or locking heads.
facts.quote: otra función posible para estas estructuras estaría en las competencias que entre los miembros de la misma especie empujándose o empalmándose, en conflictos de dominancia social y época de apareamiento.

facts.statement: The first three cervical vertebrae of Auroraceratops had fused vertebral bodies, a trait seen in more advanced ceratopsians.
facts.quote: Las tres primeras vértebras cervicales tenían los cuerpos vertebrales fusionados, como se ve en los ceratopsianos más avanzados.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Auroraceratops was found in the Xinminbao Formation, Gongpoquan Basin, in the Mazong Shan area of Gansu Province, north-central China.
facts.quote: El único espécimen conocido fue encontrado en el grupo Xinminbao, cuenca de Gongpoquan en el área de Mazong Shan, provincia de Gansu, China norcentral.

facts.statement: The type species, A. rugosus, was described by You, Li, Ji, Lamanna, and Dodson in 2005.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, A. rugosus, fue descrito por You, Li, Ji, Lamanna, y Dodson en 2005.

facts.statement: The remains were discovered by geologist Li Daqing, who presented the skull to researchers at the Fossil Development Research Center of the Third Geological and Mineral Resources Exploration in Gansu Province.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron descubiertos por el geólogo Li Daqing, que presentó el cráneo a los participantes del Centro de Investigaciones para el Desarrollo fósiles de la Tercera Exploración en Geología y Recursos Minerales de la Academia a la provincia de Gansu.

facts.statement: Remains of around 80 individuals were found in Yujingzi, northwest Gansu, providing a nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: En Yujingzi en el noroeste de Gansu se encontraron los restos de un total de alrededor de 80 individuos, por lo que es conocido por su esqueleto completo.

facts.statement: The genus name Auroraceratops comes from the Latin word 'aurora' meaning 'dawn', referring to its primitive nature, and honors Dawn Dodson, wife of describer Peter Dodson.
facts.quote: El nombre del género proviene del término latino aurora, "amanecer", en referencia a que es un ceratopsiano primitivo, y también por Dawn Dodson, esposa de Peter Dodson, uno de los paleontólogos que lo describieron.

facts.statement: The specific epithet 'rugosus' refers to the various rugose areas on the skull and jaw surface, such as the wrinkled extension of the lacrimal bone, which is distinctive of this animal.
facts.quote: El epíteto específico, "rugosus" , del latín para "rugoso", refiere a las varias áreas rugosas en la superficie del cráneo y de la mandíbula, como la extensión arrugada del hueso lagrimal, algo distintivo de este animal.

facts.statement: The type specimen, IG-2004-VD-001, consists of an almost complete skull of a subadult lacking only the rostral bone and parietal crest.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo, IG-2004-VD-001, consiste en un cráneo casi completo de un subadulto que carece solamente del hueso rostral y la cresta parietal.

facts.statement: Authors determined that Auroraceratops is a taxon sister to Coronosauria, considered the node between Protoceratopsidae and Ceratopsoidea.
facts.quote: Los autores determinaron que se trata de un taxón hermano a Coronosauria, que se puede considerar como el nodo entre Protoceratopsidae y Ceratopsoidea.

facts.statement: In 2015, VanBuren et al. placed Auroraceratops in a third group, consecutive but outside the clade formed by ceratopsians after Protoceratops and Leptoceratops.
facts.quote: VanBuren et al., en 2015, presentaron en un cladograma simplificado donde Auroraceratops aparece en un tercer grupo, consecutivo pero por fuera del clado formado por los ceratópsidos después Protoceratops y Leptoceratops.

facts.statement: Some authors define Neoceratopsia as a clade containing the last common ancestor of Auroraceratops and Triceratops and all descendants, characterized by a fusion of the first three cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los autores definen incluso a Neoceratopsia como un clado que contiene el último ancestro común de Auroraceratops y Triceratops, así como todos sus descendientes, en el cual según los autores hubo una fusión de las tres primeras vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops remains were found in Lower Cretaceous sediments of the Xinminpu Formation in the Gongpoquan Basin, Mazong Shan, Gansu Province, northeast China.
facts.quote: Los restos de Auroraceratops fueron descubiertos en sedimentos del Cretácico Inferior del grupo Xinminpu de la Cuenca Gongpoquan en Mazong Shan dentro de la provincia de Gansu, en el noreste de China.

facts.statement: During the Early Cretaceous, the region where Auroraceratops lived had a fairly dry subtropical climate.
facts.quote: En el Cretácico temprano la zona tenía un clima subtropical bastante seco.

facts.statement: Auroraceratops lived during the Albian stage, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 110.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: Auroraceratops belongs to the parent group Neoceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neoceratopsia

facts.statement: Auroraceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
